title: Dental Infections Presenting in General Practice
summary: GPs should not routinely be involved in dental treatment. Dental infections should be assessed by a qualified dental practitioner as soon as possible. An antibiotic prescription is a temporary measure which should only be provided when clinically indicated and by someone who feels competent to assess the problem.
changeSummary: Initial transcription from Eolas Medical, Northern Ireland Primary Care Antimicrobial Guidelines (v5.119.0).
clinicalNotes: Out-of-hours dental treatment is appropriate in the following situations: dental swelling (spreading infection); trauma to teeth arising from an external force; uncontrolled bleeding following extraction; severe dental pain not controlled by over-the-counter medications.

Patients can contact their own dentist if currently registered with a practice for out-of-hours arrangements. Emergency dental clinics can be contacted on weekends and bank holidays: telephone (028) 2566 3510, opening times 8:00am–12:00 noon. Further information on accessing emergency dental treatment is available on HSC online.

regimens.label: Refer to dental practitioner – no drug regimen on this page
notes: For dental abscess requiring urgent treatment, see the Dental Abscess pathway.

clinicalValidation.reviewNotes: Transcribed from Eolas Medical; not yet clinically validated. Source has no drug regimen.
